adult._note: From on-disk results/laftr_benchmark/adult/. Mean R²_onehot across all (failing) cells is 0.381 — not reported here since the column is depth-of-compliance on passing cells, which is undefined when none pass.

hmda._note_strict_pass: Submitted paper Appendix Q Table 13: LAFTR fails strict R²<0.05 on all 18 HMDA cells (mean R²_onehot 0.270 across all cells, all three purposes failing).
hmda._note_mean_r2_on_passing: Null because n_passing=0 — depth-of-compliance is only defined over passing cells.
hmda._note_task_acc: Null because the submitted paper does not report a single clean LAFTR-Q HMDA task-accuracy number under the same ledger as the strict-pass/mean-R² columns (Appendix Q reports compliance metrics; task accuracy under the LAFTR objective on HMDA is not isolated as a comparable scalar). Aggregator renders this as '—'.

diabetes._note_strict_pass: Submitted paper Appendix Q Table 13: LAFTR passes R²<0.05 on 15/18 Diabetes cells, but this is 'compliance via representation collapse' — task signal collapses with the adversarial signal.
diabetes._note_mean_r2_on_passing: Paper does not break out the depth-of-compliance for the 15 passing Diabetes cells; null with aggregator rendering '—'. The strict-pass count alone is the apples-to-apples comparison reviewers care about.
diabetes._note_task_acc: Submitted paper Appendix P: 'task accuracy 31.3% vs majority baseline 28%' — LAFTR-Q Diabetes accuracy degrades to ≈ majority baseline, confirming collapse. The 15/18 strict-pass count is thus misleading without this context; the rebuttal table caption should reference the collapse footnote when this row is cited.
